name: Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: 10 years of legal and continuous residence in Austria, of which at least 5 years must be on a residence permit (not merely tolerated stay).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 10 years of legal continuous residence, at least 5 on a residence permit.

requirements.blocker_text: Stable and regular resources of one's own (employment, income, maintenance claims, or insurance benefits) averaged over 36 months during the last 6 years before application.

Completion of the integration course/values course (Wertekurs) and a citizenship test covering basic democratic-system and Austrian-history knowledge, with exemptions for German native speakers or relevant Austrian schooling.
'Irreproachable integrity' -- no criminal convictions, no pending criminal proceedings, no serious administrative violations, and a positive attitude towards the Republic of Austria.

Applicants must in principle renounce their prior nationality; dual citizenship is not permitted through standard naturalisation (narrow exceptions exist elsewhere in the dataset's separate marriage/descent files, e.g. Nazi-persecution descendants).

Reduced to 6 years of residence if the applicant shows B2-level German, OR B1-level German plus documented personal integration efforts including at least 3 years of voluntary work/activity in the social field. This reduced-period figure is sourced only from a tier-3 monitoring report, not independently confirmed against a tier-1 Austrian government citation in this pass -- treat as indicative, not certain.

evidence_required.document: Proof of stable income over 36 of the last 72 months
Wertekurs completion certificate and citizenship test pass

sources.title: migration.gv.at -- Citizenship: standard 10-year legal continuous residence with at least 5 years on a residence permit; dual citizenship generally not permitted; jus sanguinis descent rules
oesterreich.gv.at -- General conditions for naturalisation: income (36 of last 72 months), B1 German, Wertekurs/history test, irreproachable integrity, renunciation of prior citizenship

Asylum Information Database (ECRE) -- Austria naturalisation: 6-year reduced period for exceptional integration (B2 German, or B1 + 3 years' documented volunteer work), 10-year track for recognized refugees, 15-year track for subsidiary protection beneficiaries

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Austria). The two tier-1 government pages fetched in this pass confirm the standard 10-year/5-year-permit residence figure and the general conditions (income, language, civics, conduct, renunciation) but do NOT state the 6-year exceptional-integration reduced period in numeric terms -- that figure is sourced to the tier-3 Asylum Information Database (ECRE), a recognized EU-funded monitoring consortium, not an independent Austrian government citation, so the exceptional-integration requirement group carries weaker sourcing than the standard track despite the file overall being published (the standard track alone is fully tier-1 and is sufficient for a real, usable route). Recognized refugees naturalise on the SAME 10-year clock as the standard track per this source (not a reduced track); subsidiary-protection beneficiaries face an extended 15-year clock -- neither modeled as a separate file since they use the same requirement structure as the standard/exceptional tracks, just a different residence-length gate tied to protection status (see at_international_protection.json).
